name: Fleet workers on a remote host
status_reason: First real lane (MDTWII WS350, docs) ran end to end 2026-10-13. Host sandbox, caps and no-push landing added 2026-10-13 and pass the stub-ssh suites; not yet run on the live server.
description: fleet spawn --host runs a worker on a server over ssh, inside Claude's Bash sandbox and a systemd CPU/memory scope, with Edit deny rules on the server deny list. The Mac roster stays authoritative: the worker commits locally and reports to a server outbox and, through its mail hook, to the master by mail (fleet watch applies it; fleet sync pulls the files by hand or while the mailbox is down), land fetches the lane from the fleet clone and refuses diffs outside claims.
purpose: Run fleet lanes on a server (own CPU, optionally its own Claude account) without giving the server any key into the Mac: all connections go Mac to server.

sources.claim: _spawn_remote: preflight (incl. bwrap, socat, systemd-run --user probes; 66 unless FLEET_REMOTE_UNSANDBOXED=1), base push, remote worktree, kit ship and launch in a capped scope; cleans up on failure

_spawn_remote_settings builds the --settings JSON: sandbox on with no unsandboxed fallback, writes limited to worktree, fleet clone and outbox, unix sockets blocked, Edit deny rules for the server deny list
_fleet_pane_state reports alive, dead or unreachable; an ssh failure is never dead
remote_land fetches the lane from the server fleet clone over ssh, refuses any diff outside the row's claims, and records the lane tip in lane_sha
remote-worker.sh commit stages claimed paths only, commits locally on fleet/<WS> and never pushes
host-setup creates ~/git/<name>.git and ~/fleet-repos/<name>, never touching existing server checkouts
fleet_project_name names the project after the main checkout, also from a linked worktree

unknowns: Live server not yet exercised with the sandbox: whether bypassPermissions plus sandbox stalls on network or permission prompts, whether glob denyWrite entries (from the /tmp Edit rules) are honoured by the Linux sandbox, and whether docker.sock is unreachable in practice
Workers run as the server user, which is in the docker group; only the sandbox's unix-socket block keeps docker out of reach
Edit and Write are fenced only by the deny list, not by the Bash sandbox
